reference.source: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics / relevant specialty textbook
clinicalPearls: A combined vascular malformation and overgrowth disorder, most often caused by a postzygotic mosaic activating variant in PIK3CA and placed within the PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum
Classic triad comprises a capillary malformation (port-wine stain), venous and/or lymphatic malformation, and limb overgrowth, usually affecting one lower limb
Persistent embryonic lateral (marginal) veins and deep venous anomalies predispose to venous insufficiency and thromboembolism
Limb-length and girth discrepancy can cause gait disturbance, scoliosis and orthopaedic complications requiring monitoring through growth
Lymphatic malformations may cause recurrent cellulitis, lymphatic vesicles and leakage
The presence of significant arteriovenous fistulae suggests Parkes-Weber syndrome, a related but distinct high-flow entity with different management
Care is multidisciplinary, with compression, orthopaedic and interventional radiology input, and targeted mTOR/PI3K pathway inhibitors used in selected severe cases
reference.pathophysiology: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome is largely driven by somatic mosaic activating variants in PIK3CA, which encodes the catalytic subunit of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase. Because the variant arises after fertilisation, only a proportion of cells are affected, producing the segmental and asymmetric pattern of disease. Constitutive activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway promotes tissue growth and abnormal vascular development, giving rise to the combined capillary, venous and lymphatic malformations and the overgrowth of soft tissue and bone. Anomalous and persistent embryonic veins contribute to venous hypertension and thrombotic risk. The disorder is sporadic and not inherited.
additionalDifferentials: Parkes-Weber syndrome (high-flow arteriovenous malformations with overgrowth)
CLOVES syndrome and other PIK3CA-related overgrowth phenotypes
Sturge-Weber syndrome with facial capillary malformation
Maffucci syndrome with vascular malformations and enchondromas
additionalInvestigations: Targeted molecular testing for a mosaic PIK3CA variant on affected tissue where available
Duplex ultrasound to map venous anatomy and detect deep venous anomalies or thrombosis
MRI/MR venography to delineate the extent of vascular malformation and soft-tissue overgrowth
Serial limb-length and orthopaedic assessment through childhood
Coagulation studies (including D-dimer and fibrinogen) to assess localised intravascular coagulopathy
Lymphoscintigraphy where lymphatic malformation is prominent
redFlags: Signs of deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism arising from venous anomalies
Evidence of arteriovenous fistulae or high-output cardiac features suggesting Parkes-Weber syndrome
Severe or recurrent bleeding from vascular malformations or gastrointestinal/pelvic involvement
Recurrent cellulitis or rapidly worsening limb function and deformity
reference.prognosis: Most affected individuals have a normal life expectancy, but chronic pain, venous insufficiency, orthopaedic problems and recurrent infections cause significant long-term morbidity. Thromboembolic complications and, in some, extensive malformations are the principal serious risks, and targeted pathway inhibitors offer benefit in severe disease.
pitfalls: Failing to distinguish Klippel-Trenaunay (low-flow) from Parkes-Weber (high-flow) disease, which changes management
Overlooking localised intravascular coagulopathy and thromboembolic risk before procedures
Neglecting orthopaedic surveillance for progressive limb-length discrepancy and scoliosis
Intervening on anomalous superficial veins without confirming adequate deep venous drainage
references: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics
management: Conservative venous and lymphatic care with graduated compression garments for venous insufficiency and lymphoedema
Targeted pathway-directed therapy with the mTOR inhibitor sirolimus, or a PIK3CA inhibitor such as alpelisib, for extensive or complicated malformations
Sclerotherapy, endovenous laser ablation or surgical treatment of symptomatic venous or lymphatic malformations and persistent marginal veins
Thromboprophylaxis and anticoagulation for venous thromboembolism and localised intravascular coagulopathy, particularly around surgery
Prompt antibiotic treatment of recurrent cellulitis complicating lymphatic malformation
Orthopaedic monitoring of limb-length discrepancy with shoe raises or epiphysiodesis, and management of scoliosis and gait disturbance
Genetic counselling explaining the sporadic, postzygotic mosaic PIK3CA origin
Multidisciplinary vascular anomalies team with pain management
